newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends below $1,700, watches NY spin.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends below $1,700, watches NY spin.

text.p: Origin offers shaved gains in Robusta coffee futures on Friday as market participants stood bewildered at New York's nervous gyrations.
"In New York it's really a casino today," said one trader, explaining the frequent shifts in direction by lack of follow through after waves of stop loss buying and roaster fixation.
"It's churning close to the top but we're not predicting where the top is," commented the trader.
London seemed more restrained in its action, allowing the arbitrage between Robusta and Arabica widen to an extortionate 105 cents per lb basis March from 40 cents in December.
Traders said London had managed to escape from New York's orbit and was observing its own supply and demand fundamentals.
After touching an intraday high of $1,705, benchmark May succumbed to a level below the $1,700 mark, ending at $1,675 a tonne, up $15 on the day. Turnover totalled a relatively modest 7,320 lots.
Nerves were strained on Friday before a long weekend in the United States on Monday which traders said could leave the market vulnerable to profit taking.
"The jobbers seem to take a few profits but it's not too spectacular. I would say going to the weekend no-one is going to have a position - Monday could be a pretty crazy day," said one.
March/May saw activity at $20 against $22 on Thursday.
New York prices were see-sawing ahead of midday, reeling from contract highs after a bout of speculative profit-taking and options-related selling.

But sentiment remained bullish and traders said the market could retest the 21-month highs above 180 cents basis March. There was also some squaring of positions ahead of March's first notice day February 20.
The market was likely to be supported by the ongoing strike in Colombia after 17 hours of heated bargaining between union leaders and government ministers ended in a deadlock on Thursday.
No date was set for a resumption of negotiations and the strike threatened to drag on indefinitely.

In other news, German coffee roaster Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) said it could not rule out further retail price increases if the rally in futures prices was maintained. Its two marks/kilo hike announced on February 8 no longer looked sufficient, it said.
